deals.headline: Arctos increases Lightning stake at $1.4bn control value
deals.summary: Vinik sold a further stake to Arctos Sports Partners at a deal implying a $1.4 billion control value; the sale needed a league waiver because it exceeded the NHL cap limiting a single private-equity fund to 20% of a franchise. Exact stake not stated.

deals.headline: Blue Owl co-CEOs buy just over half of the Lightning at $1.8bn
deals.investor: Group led by Doug Ostrover and Marc Lipschultz
deals.seller: Jeff Vinik; Arctos Partners (part of its interest)
deals.summary: Ostrover and Lipschultz (co-CEOs of Blue Owl Capital, investing personally) lead a group buying just over 50% of the Lightning and Vinik Sports Group at a $1.8 billion valuation, per Sportico; Vinik keeps control for three years before it transfers. Arctos sold part of its interest alongside Vinik and stays a minority partner. Terms not disclosed by the team.

name: Tampa Bay Lightning
notes: Revenue, operating income (EBITDA) and player expenses are Forbes estimates for 2024-25 (USD, net of revenue sharing and arena debt service); valuation is Forbes enterprise value calculated December 2025 (Forbes lists owners Lipschultz, Vinik, Ostrover; purchased 2010 and 2024 for $93M and $1.8B). Stakes: Sportico reports Ostrover and Lipschultz buying 'just over 50%' (not an exact figure, so stake_pct null); Arctos' percentage is not stated (the 2023 sale exceeded the NHL's 20% single-fund cap, which needed a waiver). Ostrover and Lipschultz invest personally, not through Blue Owl, so they are not flagged institutional. Arena capacity 19,092 is from the Oct 2024 release, when the building was AMALIE Arena; Benchmark International took over naming rights in August 2025 (Forbes). Hillsborough County as the public owner is not named on a page read. Missing: social, attendance, sponsors, Arctos stake %.

ownership_summary: Jeff Vinik bought the Lightning in 2010. In October 2024 a group led by Blue Owl Capital co-CEOs Doug Ostrover and Marc Lipschultz bought just over 50% at a $1.8 billion valuation (reported by Sportico); Vinik keeps control and stays governor until control passes to Ostrover and Lipschultz after three years (late 2027). Arctos Partners, a minority investor since late 2021 that increased its stake in 2023, sold part of its interest in the 2024 deal and remains a minority partner.
